title: Optimize CPU request path: reduce serialization, thread-pool contention, and enable thread pinning
author: Alex Morgan
description: Motivation: Production workloads showed persistent CPU-side bottlenecks on the host request path even when GPU inference was healthy. Hotspots were serialization/deserialization, global thread-pool contention during batching and scheduling, and KV cache lookup contention causing tail latency spikes. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to reduce per-request CPU cost and improve p95/p99 latency under realistic throughput. Approach summary: 1) Fast-path binary framing: introduce a compact TLV-style binary frame for the common sync/streaming request/response path to avoid JSON marshalling allocations and string parsing on the hot path. This is opt-in via feature flag and falls back to JSON for compatibility. 2) Per-worker request queues & thread pools: replace the single global request worker pool with per-CPU worker pools keyed to routing groups. Each pool has a low-overhead MPMC queue and bounded workers to reduce OS scheduling churn. 3) Thread pinning and NUMA-aware allocation: on platforms that expose cpu topology we pin worker threads to CPU sets (configurable via runtime feature flag) and prefer NUMA-local arenas for large allocations used by batching and KV cache. 4) Sharded KV cache read paths: split the in-memory KV cache into 32 shards with lock stripping and a lock-free fast-path (read-copy-update style) for hits; misses take a light-weight shard lock to populate cache. 5) Preallocated request arenas: allocate per-worker arenas for serialization buffers and temporary metadata to eliminate repeated malloc/free in steady-state. 6) Reduce synchronous work: move signature verification and auth checks to a small set of background verifier threads for large payloads and short-circuit common token-based ops in the fast-path. 7) Continuous batching scheduling improvements: scheduler now accounts for worker-local queue depth and latency SLOs (dynamic batch deadlines) to avoid head-of-line blocking caused by cross-pool stealing. Checklist: - [x] Implement TLV framing and compatibility fallback - [x] Add per-worker pools and MPMC queues - [x] Add thread pinning config and NUMA allocator hints - [x] Implement sharded KV cache fast-path - [x] Add arena allocator for request buffers - [x] Integrate background verifier threads - [x] Update telemetry & perf-canary tests - [x] Add feature flags and runtime knobs for gradual rollout Benchmarks and results: Microbench (synthetic single-model, 8k token sequences, 200 concurrent requests): - End-to-end p95 latency reduced from 210ms to 162ms (-22.8%) on c5-like CPU hosts - p99 improved from 390ms to 312ms (-20%) - CPU user-time per request reduced ~12% due to avoided allocations and shorter critical sections - Sustained throughput increased ~18% before GPU became the bottleneck Observability: telemetry added for: per-pool queue depth, per-shard KV cache hit/miss latencies, pinned-thread cpu usage, arena alloc counts, and batch formation latency. Perf-canary: new canary job that runs representative HTTP + streaming load tests and validates p95/p99 against baseline. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime knob and defaulted off for small customers. Gradual staged rollout starting with internal dedicated clusters, then beta customers, then all hosted traffic. Migration notes: compatibility maintained via JSON fallback. Rolling restart required for enabling thread pinning and NUMA hints. Risk: thread pinning may regress on noisy multi-tenant nodes; knob can be disabled cluster-wide. Related work: ENG-4820 (KV cache sharding), ENG-4891 (batching scheduler refactor), SUP-3345 customer incident root cause analysis.
commits: Add TLV fast-path framing and compatibility fallback
Introduce per-worker MPMC pools and worker arenas
Add NUMA-aware allocator hints and thread pinning support
Shard KV cache and implement lock-free fast-path
Move heavy auth checks to verifier threads
Telemetry and perf-canary jobs for CPU path

Priya: Can we measure the latency impact when pinning is enabled on our multi-tenant clusters? Suggest adding a knob to disable pinning per-cluster.
Author: Added cluster-level knob and unit tests; added note in rollout doc.

Samir: The TLV framing looks good but please ensure we maintain backwards compat with existing API clients.
Author: TLV is feature-flagged and has JSON fallback; updated docs and added integration tests.

Evelyn: Sharded KV cache complexity is higher; any memory overhead?
Author: Added sizing heuristic: shards only allocate on demand and we expose a per-shard memory cap. Added metrics to alert on total memory used by KV cache.
release_notes: Runtime: Reduce CPU-side request path latency by optimizing serialization, introducing per-worker thread pools, sharded KV cache fast-paths, and optional thread pinning/NUMA hints. Improves p95/p99 latency and throughput for high-concurrency workloads. Feature-flagged; rolling restart required to enable pinning.
